In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

u = 2.2544 m/s ± 1% (the speed of the cart at the start of phase 1). The acceleration of the cart during phase 1, a1, equals 60.459 cm/s^2 ± 1%. The duration of phase 2 is t2 = 1.4577 min ± 2%. The speed of the cart at the end of phase 1, v, equals 12.876 km/h ± 1%. The braking time in phase 3 is t3 = 0.079132 min ± 1%. The width of the track is w_track = 551.86 mm ± 1%.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

text:

At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

target_desc: magnitude of the applied pulling force
text:
A crate of mass m rests on a level floor, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is mu. Starting from rest, the crate is pulled by a constant horizontal force F for a time t1. While it slides, the floor exerts a normal force N and a kinetic friction force f_k on it; the net horizontal force on the crate is F_net and its acceleration is a1. When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

The momentum of the crate when the pull stops is p = 716.89 N s ± 1%. It is known that F_net = 339.78 N ± 1%, where F_net is the net horizontal force on the crate during the pull. The height of the crate is h_crate = 0.54922 m ± 1%. The magnitude of the crate's deceleration after the pull, a2, equals 1.4219 m/s^2 ± 5%. len_rope = 4468.2 mm ± 1% (the length of the rope used to pull the crate). t2 = 4.8083 s ± 1% (the time the crate slides after the pull before stopping). Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

Determine F, the magnitude of the applied pulling force. Express the result in N. Report these intermediate quantities in <steps>: v, m, f_k.

target_desc: maximum compression of the spring
text:
Starting from rest at a height h, a block of mass m slides down a frictionless ramp; U denotes its potential energy at the top relative to the bottom. At the bottom it has kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. Next it slides across a rough level section of length L (coefficient of kinetic friction mu), losing energy W_f to friction, and exits with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. On the frictionless floor beyond, it hits a light spring of spring constant k, which it compresses by at most x; at that maximum compression the spring exerts a force of magnitude F_s on the block.

The speed of the block after the rough patch is v2 = 3.2628 m/s ± 1%. It is known that U = 0.039118 kJ ± 1%, where U is the gravitational potential energy of the block at the top. The spring constant is k = 6167.1 N/m ± 5%. v1 = 367.99 cm/s ± 1% (the speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp). Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

target_desc: braking time in phase 3
text:
A cart moves along a straight, level track in three phases. In phase 1 it starts with speed u and accelerates uniformly with acceleration a1 for a time t1, covering a distance s1 and reaching speed v. In phase 2 it moves at the constant speed v for a time t2, covering a distance s2. In phase 3 it brakes with a constant deceleration of magnitude b until it comes to rest, which takes a time t3 and covers a distance s3. Over the whole trip the cart covers a total distance d_tot in a total time t_tot, so its average speed is v_avg.

Known values:
- The distance covered during phase 1, s1, equals 124.86 m ± 5%.
- The total duration of the trip is t_tot = 0.017738 h ± 1%.
- The braking distance in phase 3 is s3 = 384.52 m ± 1%.
- The average speed of the cart over the whole trip, v_avg, equals 45.661 km/h ± 1%.
- The duration of phase 2 is t2 = 0.26632 min ± 1%.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

What is the braking time in phase 3, t3? Give your answer in h. Report these intermediate quantities in <steps>: d_tot, s2, v.

target_desc: mass of the crate
text:
On a horizontal floor sits a crate of mass m; mu is the coefficient of kinetic friction between crate and floor. A constant horizontal pull F acts on the initially resting crate for a time t1. During the motion the normal force is N, the kinetic friction force is f_k, the net force is F_net and the acceleration is a1. At the moment the pull is removed, the crate moves with speed v, carries momentum p, and has covered a distance s1. Friction then decelerates it at a rate a2 (magnitude) until it comes to rest after an extra time t2, covering an extra distance s2.

The kinetic friction force on the crate is f_k = 0.43141 kN ± 1%. It is known that p = 707.80 kg m/s ± 1%, where p is the momentum of the crate when the pull stops. It is known that F = 0.60402 kN ± 2%, where F is the magnitude of the applied pulling force. The distance the crate moves during the pull, s1, equals 951.90 cm ± 1%. It is known that len_rope = 67.381 cm ± 1%, where len_rope is the length of the rope used to pull the crate. h_crate = 33.095 cm ± 1% (the height of the crate). Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

Find the mass of the crate, m, in kg. In <steps>, report the intermediate values F_net, t1, v.

target_desc: mass of the block
text:
A block of mass m is released from rest at height h on a frictionless ramp. At the top, its gravitational potential energy relative to the bottom of the ramp is U. It slides down and reaches the bottom with kinetic energy K1 and speed v1. It then crosses a rough horizontal patch of length L where the coefficient of kinetic friction is mu; friction does work of magnitude W_f on the block, which leaves the patch with kinetic energy K2 and speed v2. Finally, on a frictionless floor, the block runs into a light horizontal spring with spring constant k and compresses it by a maximum distance x, at which moment the spring force on the block has magnitude F_s.

Known values:
- It is known that F_s = 0.12485 kN ± 1%, where F_s is the magnitude of the spring force at maximum compression.
- The spring constant is k = 3.5752 N/cm ± 1%.
- The speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp is v1 = 25.543 km/h ± 1%.
- len_spring = 0.30591 m ± 1% (the natural length of the spring).
- The magnitude of the work done by friction on the rough patch, W_f, equals 6303.3 mJ ± 2%.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

What is the mass of the block, m? Give your answer in g. In <steps>, report the intermediate values x, K2, K1.

target_desc: distance covered during phase 2
text:
Consider a cart on a straight, horizontal track. Phase 1: the cart has initial speed u and speeds up with constant acceleration a1 during a time t1; it travels s1 and ends the phase with speed v. Phase 2: the cart keeps the constant speed v for a time t2 and travels s2. Phase 3: the cart slows down with constant deceleration of magnitude b and stops after a time t3, having travelled s3 in this phase. For the entire motion, d_tot is the total distance, t_tot the total time, and v_avg the average speed.

The duration of phase 1 is t1 = 0.26018 min ± 1%. t2 = 0.18887 min ± 2% (the duration of phase 2). It is known that v_avg = 835.67 cm/s ± 1%, where v_avg is the average speed of the cart over the whole trip. b = 143.99 cm/s^2 ± 1% (the magnitude of the braking deceleration in phase 3). d_tot = 292.91 m ± 1% (the total distance covered by the cart).

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

When the pull stops, the crate has speed v and momentum p, and it has moved a distance s1. Afterwards it slides freely, slowing down under friction alone with a deceleration of magnitude a2, and stops after a further time t2 and distance s2.

- The momentum of the crate when the pull stops, p, equals 8.1919 kg m/s ± 1%.
- The distance the crate slides after the pull, s2, equals 5044.6 mm ± 1%.
- The net horizontal force on the crate during the pull, F_net, equals 1.1635 N ± 2%.
- It is known that m = 1916.4 g ± 1%, where m is the mass of the crate.
- Use g = 9.81 m/s^2.

Values marked ± p% are measurements: p% is the relative standard uncertainty (one standard deviation) of that measurement. Values without ± are exact.

Determine F, the magnitude of the applied pulling force. Express the result in N. In <steps>, report the intermediate values v, a2, f_k.
